page: Vultr voc-m-16c-128gb-1600s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance equipped with 16 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs derived from 8 physical AMD EPYC cores running at a base clock of 2.0 GHz. Each physical core supports two hardware threads, backed by 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache. The architecture includes hardware support for AVX, AES, SHA-NI, and BMI2 instruction sets, though it lacks AVX-512 extensions. Memory capacity is substantial at 128.0 GB of RAM, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU ratio. A 1600 GB NVMe SSD is bundled directly with the configuration, accompanied by one complimentary public IPv4 address, with no hardware GPU acceleration present.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong memory and single-core computational characteristics. In stress-ng single-core tests, the processor achieves a score of 3207.88, landing in the top 10 percent of evaluated systems, whereas multi-core execution registers an average 50139.7. PassMark evaluates overall memory performance at 2935.37, placing it in the top 25 percent tier, reinforced by uncached large-block read throughput of 131.64 GB/s and write throughput of 67.64 GB/s. Software compilation under Clang scores 19388.0 on Geekbench, with static web throughput achieving 16.6 GB/s and Redis processing reaching 30.71 million SET operations per second.

The 1:8 compute-to-memory configuration delivers high resource density for workloads requiring vast RAM pools without necessitating hyper-dense core counts. Bundling 1600 GB of NVMe SSD directly on the instance avoids external volume network bottlenecks, offering solid qualitative cost efficiency for input-output demanding setups. The primary tradeoff lies in the moderate 2.0 GHz base clock speed and absence of AVX-512 instructions, which limits raw vector math acceleration. The platform is best suited for memory-resident caching clusters, relational database management systems, data processing pipelines, and enterprise backend services.
description: Vultr voc-m-16c-128gb-1600s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute virtual machine provisioned with 16 dedicated AMD EPYC vCPUs across 8 physical cores at 2.0 GHz, 128.0 GB of system memory, and a bundled 1600 GB local NVMe SSD. The processor features AVX, AES, and SHA-NI instruction support without AVX-512 or dedicated GPU hardware. Benchmarks highlight upper-tier single-core execution alongside strong memory throughput, scoring in the top quartile of PassMark memory evaluations and delivering 30.71 million Redis SET operations per second. With an 8 GB RAM per vCPU allocation, this configuration offers high memory density relative to processing cores, optimizing qualitative operating costs for large-footprint applications. The system is well configured for production relational databases, in-memory key-value stores, enterprise application backends, and intensive extract-transform-load data pipelines.
